questions.text: The enzyme pepsin digests proteins most effectively in:
options: (A) the alkaline medium of the small intestine
(B) the acidic medium of the stomach
(C) the neutral medium of the mouth
(D) the alkaline medium of the large intestine

questions.text: Oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs first enters which chamber of the human heart?
The opening and closing of a stomatal pore is brought about by the change in shape of:
Which of the following shows the correct path of air during inhalation in humans?
options: (A) Nostrils → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → alveoli
(B) Nostrils → larynx → pharynx → bronchi → trachea → alveoli
(C) Nostrils → trachea → pharynx → larynx → alveoli → bronchi
(D) Nostrils → pharynx → trachea → larynx → bronchi → alveoli

questions.text: The structural and functional unit of the human kidney, where urine is formed, is the:
The tiny gap across which a nerve impulse passes from one neuron to the next is called a:
Which plant hormone mainly promotes cell division and is present in high concentration in fruits and seeds?
Iodised salt is recommended in our diet because iodine is needed for the synthesis of:

After fertilisation in a flowering plant, the seed develops from the:
Which of the following sexually transmitted diseases is caused by bacteria?

In human beings, whether a child will be a boy or a girl is decided by:
options: (A) the sex chromosome present in the mother's egg
(B) the diet of the mother during pregnancy

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct food chain?
If 10,000 J of energy is available at the producer level of a food chain, the energy available to the secondary consumers will be about:

Assertion (A): Arteries have thick and elastic walls.
Reason (R): Blood flows through the arteries under high pressure as it is pumped out of the heart.

Assertion (A): Insulin helps in regulating the level of sugar in the blood.
Reason (R): Insulin is secreted by the thyroid gland.

Assertion (A): Plants raised by vegetative propagation are genetically similar to the parent plant.
Reason (R): Vegetative propagation involves the fusion of male and female gametes.

Assertion (A): The use of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) is being reduced all over the world.
Reason (R): A molecule of ozone is made up of three atoms of oxygen.
Why is the rate of breathing in aquatic organisms much faster than that in terrestrial organisms? Give one reason.
State two differences between the transport of materials in xylem and in phloem.
Name the plant hormone responsible for (a) the elongation of the stem and (b) the wilting of leaves. State one more function of each.
What is the role of the seminal vesicles and the prostate gland in the human male reproductive system?
How did Mendel's experiments with pea plants show that a trait may be dominant or recessive? Explain with one example.
Why are substances like polythene bags called non-biodegradable? State two ways in which they harm the environment.
Describe the digestion of food in the small intestine of human beings. In your answer, state the role of (a) bile juice, (b) pancreatic juice and (c) villi.
How is the movement of the leaves of the 'touch-me-not' plant different from the bending of a shoot towards light? Give three points of difference.

Describe the events that take place in a flower from the time a pollen grain lands on a suitable stigma until the formation of the zygote. What do the ovary and the ovule develop into after fertilisation?

A plant with blue flowers (BB) is crossed with a plant with white flowers (bb).
(a) What will be the colour of the flowers in the F₁ generation? Give a reason.
(b) If the F₁ plants are self-pollinated, what percentage of the F₂ plants will have white flowers?
(c) State the ratio of BB : Bb plants in the F₂ generation.

Farmers around a village pond used a pesticide on their crops for several years. Rain water carried a part of this pesticide into the pond. A study of the pond showed that the concentration of the pesticide was 0.02 ppm in water, 5 ppm in small fish and 25 ppm in the fish-eating birds living near the pond. The pesticide could not be broken down by the organisms and so it kept collecting in their bodies.
(a) Name the phenomenon shown by the rising concentration of the pesticide.
(b) Why do the birds have the highest concentration of the pesticide?
(c) Suggest two practices that farmers can adopt to reduce this problem.
OR
(c) Write a food chain of four trophic levels operating in this pond and name the organisms that form the third trophic level.

The kidneys remove nitrogenous wastes such as urea from the blood. If both kidneys of a person stop working, the wastes build up in the blood and can be fatal. Such a person is treated with an artificial kidney, a process called haemodialysis. The patient's blood is passed through long tubes with a selectively permeable lining, which are dipped in a tank of dialysing fluid. The wastes pass from the blood into this fluid and the purified blood is returned to the patient.
(a) Name the main nitrogenous waste removed by the kidneys in humans.
(b) Why should the dialysing fluid have the same concentration of salts and glucose as normal blood?
(c) State two differences between the working of a natural kidney and that of an artificial kidney.
OR
(c) Explain how the amount of water reabsorbed in the nephron changes on a hot day when a person has drunk very little water.

(a) Name the parts of the human female reproductive system where (i) eggs are produced, (ii) fertilisation takes place and (iii) the embryo is implanted.
(b) How does the embryo get its nourishment inside the mother's body?
(c) What happens when the egg is not fertilised?
OR
(a) What is contraception? List three different methods of contraception and state how each one works.
(b) Why is the use of a condom also considered important for health reasons?

(a) What is meant by double circulation of blood? Why is it necessary in human beings?
(b) Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than that of the right ventricle?
(c) State two differences between arteries and veins.
OR
(a) List the three events that occur during photosynthesis.
(b) How do desert plants take up carbon dioxide and still prevent the loss of water?
(c) Describe an activity to show that sunlight is necessary for photosynthesis.
The reaction Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu is an example of a:
Which of the following is an endothermic process?
options: (C) Decomposition of calcium carbonate on heating

questions.text: When lead nitrate is heated strongly, brown fumes are seen. These fumes are of:
Packets of potato chips are flushed with nitrogen gas in order to:
options: (B) increase the weight of the packet
(D) prevent the oil in the chips from getting oxidised

questions.text: A solution turns red litmus blue. Its pH is most likely to be:
The chemical formula of Plaster of Paris is:
Milk of magnesia, used as an antacid, is chemically:
Tooth enamel starts getting corroded when the pH in the mouth falls below:
Which of the following metals is kept under kerosene oil?
Which of the following oxides is amphoteric in nature?
Ionic compounds generally have high melting points because:
options: (B) strong electrostatic forces of attraction hold their ions together
(C) they conduct electricity in the solid state
(D) they are made up of molecules

questions.text: Brass is an alloy of:
The functional group present in propanone is:
The next higher homologue of C₃H₇OH is:
The total number of covalent bonds present in a molecule of ethane (C₂H₆) is:
When ethanol reacts with sodium metal, the products formed are:

Assertion (A): White silver chloride turns grey when it is kept in sunlight.
Reason (R): Silver chloride decomposes into silver and chlorine in the presence of sunlight.

Assertion (A): Dry hydrogen chloride gas does not change the colour of dry blue litmus paper.
Reason (R): Hydrogen chloride produces hydrogen ions only in the presence of water.

Assertion (A): Gold and platinum occur in the free state in nature.
Reason (R): Gold and platinum are highly reactive metals.

Assertion (A): Soaps do not form lather easily with hard water.
Reason (R): Hard water contains calcium and magnesium salts, which react with soap to form an insoluble scum.

A milkman adds a very small amount of baking soda to fresh milk.
(a) Why does he shift the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline?
(b) Why does this milk take a longer time to set as curd?

Give reasons for the following:
(a) Ionic compounds conduct electricity in the molten state but not in the solid state.
(b) Metals are used for making school bells.

Write balanced chemical equations for the following reactions and name the type of each reaction:
(a) Barium chloride solution is mixed with sodium sulphate solution.
(b) Zinc granules are added to dilute sulphuric acid.
(c) Ferrous sulphate crystals are heated strongly.

(a) What is the chlor-alkali process? Write the chemical equation of the reaction involved.
(b) Name the gas produced at the anode and the gas produced at the cathode in this process.
(c) State one use of each of these two gases.

A metal M occurs in nature as its carbonate ore, MCO₃. The metal lies in the middle of the reactivity series.
(a) Name the two main steps used to obtain the metal from this ore.
(b) Write the chemical equations for these steps, taking zinc as the metal.
(c) Name the process used to refine the impure metal so obtained.

(a) Distinguish between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons on the basis of the flame they produce on burning.
(b) What is hydrogenation? Write a chemical equation to show it.
(c) State one industrial application of hydrogenation.

Three clean iron nails were kept in three test tubes for a week. Test tube P had tap water, so the nail was in contact with both air and water. Test tube Q had boiled distilled water covered with a layer of oil. Test tube R had dry air with some anhydrous calcium chloride. After a week, only the nail in test tube P had rusted. Rusting damages bridges, ships and car bodies, and a lot of money is spent every year to prevent it.
(a) What does this experiment tell us about the conditions necessary for rusting?
(b) Why was a layer of oil added in test tube Q?
(c) What is galvanisation? Why does a galvanised iron article not rust even when the zinc coating is scratched?
OR
(c) What is an alloy? Name the metals mixed with iron to make stainless steel and state how this helps.

Most dirt is oily in nature and oil does not dissolve in water. A soap molecule has two ends: a long hydrocarbon chain and an ionic end. When soap is added to water containing oily dirt, the soap molecules arrange themselves in clusters around the oil droplets. Rinsing then removes the dirt. In hard water, however, soap forms a sticky white solid and a lot of soap is wasted. Detergents were developed to overcome this problem.
(a) What name is given to the cluster of soap molecules formed around an oil droplet?
(b) Which end of the soap molecule attaches to the oil droplet and which end faces the water?
(c) Why does soap form a sticky solid (scum) with hard water? Why do detergents not form it?
OR
(c) Would a micelle be formed if soap were dissolved in ethanol instead of water? Give a reason for your answer.

(a) Write the chemical equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with ethanol in the presence of an acid catalyst. Name the reaction and the product.
(b) What is observed when ethanoic acid is added to sodium hydrogencarbonate? Write the equation.
(c) Why is pure ethanoic acid called glacial acetic acid?
(d) State one chemical test to distinguish ethanol from ethanoic acid.
OR
(a) What is a homologous series? State three characteristics of a homologous series.
(b) Draw the structures of the two isomers of butane (C₄H₁₀).
(c) Why does carbon form compounds mainly by covalent bonding?

(a) Explain the importance of pH in (i) the digestion of food in the stomach and (ii) the growth of plants in soil.
(b) What is baking powder? Write the equation for the change that takes place when it is heated or mixed with water, and explain how it makes a cake soft and spongy.
(c) What is meant by water of crystallisation? Give one example of a salt that has it.
OR
(a) How is washing soda prepared from sodium chloride? Write the chemical equations of the steps involved.
(b) State two uses of washing soda.
(c) A solution of sodium carbonate is basic. Explain why.
An object is placed 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. The image formed is:
options: (B) real, inverted and of the same size as the object

questions.text: The direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor is given by:

Assertion (A): A convex mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles.
Reason (R): A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image and gives a wider field of view.

Assertion (A): A fuse wire is made of a material that has a high melting point.
Reason (R): A fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit when the current becomes larger than the safe limit.

Assertion (A): Two magnetic field lines never cross each other.
Reason (R): Magnetic field lines are closed curves.
An object 5 cm high is placed at a distance of 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Find the position, nature and size of the image formed.

(a) State the two laws of refraction of light.
(b) The refractive index of glass is 1.5. Calculate the speed of light in glass. (Speed of light in vacuum = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
A concave mirror of focal length 15 cm forms a real image that is three times the size of the object. Calculate the distance of the object from the mirror.

questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text: Explain the formation of a rainbow in the sky with the help of a labelled diagram. Why is a rainbow always seen in the direction opposite to that of the Sun?

questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text:
(a) What is presbyopia? State its cause and how it is corrected.
(b) Why can we see the Sun about two minutes before the actual sunrise?

(a) Derive an expression for the equivalent resistance of three resistors R₁, R₂ and R₃ connected in series.
(b) Why is an ammeter always connected in series in a circuit?

An electric iron is rated 1100 W, 220 V. Calculate:
(a) the current drawn by the iron,
(b) the resistance of its heating element, and
(c) the energy consumed in kWh if it is used for 2 hours.

(a) Draw the pattern of magnetic field lines around a bar magnet.
(b) State two properties of magnetic field lines.
(c) How does a current-carrying solenoid behave like a bar magnet?

(a) State Fleming's left-hand rule.
(b) On what factors does the force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field depend?
(c) When is this force the largest?

In a house, all the appliances are connected in parallel across the live and neutral wires, and each appliance has its own switch. The supply reaches the house at 220 V. The wiring has two separate circuits, one of 5 A rating for bulbs and fans and another of 15 A rating for appliances such as geysers and air coolers. A third wire, the earth wire, is connected to the metal body of appliances such as the electric iron and the refrigerator.
(a) Why are household appliances connected in parallel and not in series? Give one reason.
(b) What is the function of the earth wire?
(c) What is overloading? State two ways in which it can be caused.
OR
(c) A geyser of 2 kW and an electric kettle of 1.5 kW are switched on together in the 15 A circuit at 220 V. Find the total current drawn and state whether the fuse will blow.

An eye specialist tests the eyesight of two patients. For the first patient, Asha, the prescription for the lens is +2.0 D. For the second patient, Imran, the prescription is −0.5 D. The power of a lens tells us how strongly it converges or diverges light, and opticians often place lenses in contact to get the required power.
(a) What type of lens is prescribed for Asha?
(b) Calculate the focal length of the lens prescribed for Imran.
(c) Define one dioptre. If lenses of power +2.0 D and −0.5 D are placed in contact, find the power and the focal length of the combination.
OR
(c) Draw a ray diagram to show how a convex lens corrects the defect of vision in which nearby objects cannot be seen clearly.

(a) State Ohm's law. Describe the shape of the V-I graph for a metallic conductor.
(b) List the factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends.
(c) A 4 Ω resistor is connected in series with a parallel combination of a 6 Ω resistor and a 3 Ω resistor. The arrangement is connected to a 6 V battery. Find (i) the total resistance of the circuit, (ii) the current drawn from the battery and (iii) the current through the 6 Ω resistor.
OR
(a) What is the heating effect of electric current? Write the expression for the heat produced in a resistor.
(b) Why is tungsten used for the filament of an electric bulb?
(c) A 100 W bulb and a 60 W bulb are connected in parallel to a 220 V supply. Find the total current drawn from the supply.

(a) Draw a ray diagram to show the image formed by a convex lens when the object is placed between F₁ and 2F₁. State the nature of the image.
(b) Write the lens formula and state the sign convention used for the object distance.
(c) An object is placed 30 cm from a concave lens of focal length 15 cm. Find the position and the magnification of the image.
OR
(a) Draw a ray diagram to show the image formed by a concave mirror when the object is placed between the pole and the principal focus. State the nature of the image.
(b) Define the radius of curvature of a spherical mirror and write its relation with the focal length.
(c) An object is placed 10 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position and nature of the image.
Which component of blood helps in the clotting of blood at the site of an injury?
The part of the human brain that maintains the posture and balance of the body is the:
Regeneration as a method of reproduction is seen in:
The number of pairs of autosomes present in a human body cell is:
Organisms that break down the dead remains and waste products of other organisms are called:
The products of anaerobic respiration in yeast are:

Assertion (A): A child who inherits a Y chromosome is a boy.
Reason (R): A child inherits one sex chromosome from each parent.

Assertion (A): Veins have valves along their length.
Reason (R): Valves ensure that the blood in the veins flows only in one direction, towards the heart.
What is a reflex arc? Name its components in the order in which the nerve impulse travels through them.
Why is the copying of DNA an essential part of reproduction? What is the importance of the small variations that arise during this copying?
How is ozone formed in the upper atmosphere? Write the reactions involved.

(a) Explain how air is taken in and given out of the lungs during breathing in human beings.
(b) State three features of the alveoli that make them suitable for the exchange of gases.

In pea plants, round seeds (R) are dominant over wrinkled seeds (r) and yellow seeds (Y) are dominant over green seeds (y). A plant with round yellow seeds (RRYY) is crossed with a plant with wrinkled green seeds (rryy).
(a) What will be the appearance of the seeds of the F₁ plants?
(b) Write the ratio of the four kinds of plants obtained in the F₂ generation.
(c) What does this cross tell us about the inheritance of two different traits?

In some hilly regions, many people were found to have a swollen neck. Doctors found that the soil and water in these regions were poor in a particular mineral, so the food grown there also lacked it. A gland in the neck needs this mineral to make its hormone. The government then started a programme to supply salt enriched with this mineral, and the number of new cases fell sharply.
(a) Name the gland and the mineral referred to in the passage.
(b) Name the hormone produced by this gland and state its function.
(c) Name the disease described here. Why is the timing and amount of hormone released by a gland so important? Explain with the example of insulin.
OR
(c) Name the hormone that is released into the blood when a person is frightened. State two changes that it brings about in the body.

(a) Name the three main regions of the human brain and state one function of each.
(b) How are the brain and the spinal cord protected in our body?
(c) State two differences between a reflex action and a voluntary action.
OR
(a) What are plant hormones? Name one hormone that promotes growth and one that inhibits growth.
(b) Explain, with the role of auxin, how a shoot bends towards light.
(c) What is meant by geotropism? How do roots and shoots respond to gravity?
Which of the following is a redox reaction?
Which of the following is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
Which of the following metals is the most reactive?

Assertion (A): Sodium reacts violently with cold water.
Reason (R): Sodium lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series.

Assertion (A): Bleaching powder gives a strong smell of chlorine when it is left open in air.
Reason (R): Bleaching powder reacts slowly with the carbon dioxide of the air to release chlorine.
Give reasons: (a) carbon compounds are generally poor conductors of electricity, and (b) most carbon compounds have low melting and boiling points.

Three solutions X, Y and Z have pH values of 2, 7 and 13 respectively.
(a) Which solution will react with zinc granules to release hydrogen gas? Write the equation, taking the acid to be dilute hydrochloric acid.
(b) Which solution will turn phenolphthalein pink?
(c) What happens when solutions X and Z are mixed? Name the type of reaction.

An organic compound A with the molecular formula C₂H₆O is used in tincture of iodine and in cough syrups. On heating with alkaline potassium permanganate, A gives compound B, a dilute solution of which is used as vinegar.
(a) Identify A and B.
(b) Write the chemical equation for the conversion of A into B.
(c) What happens when A and B are warmed together in the presence of an acid? Write the equation.

Before whitewashing the walls of his house, a painter adds lumps of quicklime to a bucket of water. The mixture becomes so hot that the water starts to bubble. He lets it stand and then applies the solution to the walls. The walls look dull at first, but two or three days later they have a bright white, shiny finish.
(a) Write the chemical equation for the reaction of quicklime with water and name the product.
(b) Is this reaction exothermic or endothermic? What type of reaction is it?
(c) Explain, with a chemical equation, why the walls become shiny two or three days after whitewashing.
OR
(c) Write the chemical formula of marble. Name the gas given out when marble reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid and write the equation.

(a) What is observed when an iron nail is kept in copper sulphate solution for some time? Write the chemical equation and state what this tells us about the reactivity of iron and copper.
(b) Show the formation of magnesium chloride by the transfer of electrons. (Atomic numbers: Mg = 12, Cl = 17)
(c) Why are sodium and potassium obtained by electrolysis and not by reduction of their oxides with carbon?
OR
(a) Distinguish between roasting and calcination with one chemical equation each.
(b) Describe the electrolytic refining of copper. Name the anode, the cathode and the electrolyte used.
(c) What is anode mud?
A convex mirror used as a rear-view mirror in a bus has a radius of curvature of 4 m. A car is 6 m behind the bus. Find the position, nature and magnification of the image of the car.

(a) Define the resistivity of a material and write its SI unit.
(b) A wire of length 2 m and area of cross-section 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m² has a resistance of 0.034 Ω. Calculate the resistivity of its material.
(c) What will be the resistance of the wire if its length is doubled, keeping the area the same?

questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text:
Give reasons for the following:
(a) Stars appear to twinkle but planets do not.
(b) Danger signal lights are red in colour.
(c) The sky appears dark to astronauts in space.

During a classroom demonstration, a teacher placed a magnetic compass near a straight copper wire connected to a battery through a switch. When the switch was closed, the compass needle moved from its position. When the terminals of the battery were interchanged, the needle moved in the opposite direction. The teacher then wound the wire into a circular loop and repeated the experiment, and the needle moved by a larger amount.
(a) What does the movement of the compass needle show?
(b) Why did the needle move in the opposite direction when the battery terminals were interchanged?
(c) How does the magnetic field due to a straight current-carrying wire change when (i) the current is increased and (ii) the compass is moved farther from the wire?
OR
(c) Why does a circular coil of n turns produce a magnetic field n times as strong as that of a single turn carrying the same current?

questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text:
(a) Draw a labelled diagram of the human eye. State the function of the iris, the ciliary muscles and the retina.
(b) What is meant by the power of accommodation of the eye?
(c) The far point of a person with myopia is 80 cm. Find the nature and the power of the lens needed to correct this defect.
OR
(a) What is dispersion of white light? Draw a diagram to show the dispersion of white light by a glass prism.
(b) Why do different colours of white light bend through different angles in a prism?
(c) How did Newton show that white light is made up of seven colours and that these colours can be recombined?
A pea plant that is heterozygous for tallness (Tt) is crossed with a dwarf pea plant (tt). The ratio of tall to dwarf plants among the offspring will be:
Which of the following characters of the pea plant was NOT among those studied by Mendel?
In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle, the frog is a:

options: (A) Grass clippings, paper and cotton cloth
(C) Polythene bag, fruit peels and wood

questions.text: After fertilisation in a flower, the fruit develops from the:
Which of the following organisms reproduces by forming spores in sporangia?
Growth hormone in the human body is secreted by the:
Which of the following organisms breaks down food material outside its body and then absorbs it?

Assertion (A): In human males, the testes are located outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum.
Reason (R): The formation of sperms requires a temperature lower than the normal body temperature.

Assertion (A): The flow of energy in an ecosystem is unidirectional.
Reason (R): Only about 1% of the energy available at one trophic level is passed on to the next trophic level.

Assertion (A): The kidneys are the main excretory organs in human beings.
Reason (R): Urine is stored in the urinary bladder until it is passed out.
What is a gene? Explain, taking the example of plant height, how a gene controls a characteristic.
What is a trophic level? Why do food chains usually have only three or four trophic levels?
Name the male and the female reproductive parts of a bisexual flower. How is cross-pollination different from self-pollination?
What are tropic movements? Give one example each of positive phototropism and negative geotropism.

(a) What is translocation in plants? Which tissue carries it out?
(b) Explain how water and minerals reach the top of a tall tree. What is the role of transpiration in this process?

(a) Describe the process of budding in Hydra.
(b) Why can complex multicellular organisms not reproduce by simple cell division, as unicellular organisms do?
(c) Name one organism that reproduces by fragmentation.

(a) Explain, with the help of a flow chart, how the sex of a child is determined in human beings.
(b) Why is it wrong to say that the mother is responsible for the sex of her child?

Ravi crossed a pure-breeding pea plant with violet flowers with a pure-breeding pea plant with white flowers. All the plants of the F₁ generation had violet flowers. He then allowed the F₁ plants to self-pollinate and raised 400 plants in the F₂ generation. Of these, 300 plants had violet flowers and 100 had white flowers.
(a) Which flower colour is dominant? Give a reason.
(b) Using V for the dominant allele and v for the recessive allele, write the genotype of the F₁ plants.
(c) How many of the 300 violet-flowered F₂ plants are expected to be pure-breeding? Explain.
OR
(c) Write the genotypic ratio of the F₂ generation and name the genotypes.

(a) What is respiration? Write two differences between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
(b) Show, with the help of a flow chart, the breakdown of glucose by different pathways in (i) yeast, (ii) our muscle cells during vigorous exercise and (iii) the mitochondria.
(c) Why do we sometimes get muscle cramps after running fast?
OR
(a) Write the balanced chemical equation for photosynthesis and list the three events that occur during this process.
(b) How do desert plants carry out gas exchange without losing too much water?
(c) Describe an experiment to show that chlorophyll is necessary for photosynthesis.
Which of the following is a double displacement reaction?
In the balanced equation a Fe + b H₂O → c Fe₃O₄ + d H₂, the values of a, b, c and d are respectively:
When dilute hydrochloric acid is added to sodium carbonate, a gas is given off that turns lime water milky. The gas is:
An aqueous solution of which of the following salts is basic?
Which of the following non-metals is a good conductor of electricity?
An element X forms an oxide X₂O. A solution of this oxide in water turns red litmus blue. The element X is most likely:
The IUPAC name of the compound CH₃CH₂CHO is:
Which of the following pairs of compounds belongs to the same homologous series?

Assertion (A): Iron gates and grills are painted to protect them from rusting.
Reason (R): A coat of paint prevents moist air from coming in contact with the surface of iron.

Assertion (A): Ethanoic acid is a strong acid.
Reason (R): Ethanoic acid turns blue litmus red.

Assertion (A): Baking powder is used to make cakes soft and spongy.
Reason (R): Sodium hydrogencarbonate is also used in soda-acid fire extinguishers.
Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned with sandpaper before burning it in air? Write the balanced chemical equation for the burning of magnesium.
What is an alloy? Why is pure gold not used for making jewellery? What is meant by 22-carat gold?

Metals differ in how they react with water.
(a) Name one metal that reacts with cold water and write the balanced equation for the reaction.
(b) Name one metal that does not react with cold or hot water but reacts with steam. Write the equation.
(c) Why does calcium start floating when it reacts with water?

(a) How is washing soda obtained from baking soda? Write the chemical equations involved.
(b) What is meant by water of crystallisation? Write the formula of washing soda and of gypsum.
(c) State one use of washing soda.
What is a decomposition reaction? Write one balanced chemical equation each for a decomposition reaction brought about by (a) heat, (b) electricity and (c) light.

While playing in the garden, Nisha was stung by a red ant and felt a sharp burning pain. Her mother quickly rubbed a paste of baking soda on the spot and the pain soon reduced. The same evening, her grandfather complained of a burning feeling in his chest after a heavy meal and took a spoonful of an antacid. Her mother explained that both remedies work on the same principle.
(a) Name the acid present in the sting of the ant.
(b) Why did the baking soda paste give relief? Name the type of reaction involved.
(c) Why does a person get a burning feeling in the stomach after overeating? Name one substance commonly used as an antacid.
OR
(c) Why are we advised to brush our teeth after eating sweets? How does toothpaste help to prevent tooth decay?

(a) Why should a chemical equation always be balanced?
(b) Write the balanced chemical equations for the following and state the type of each reaction:
(i) Aluminium reacts with copper chloride to give aluminium chloride and copper.
(ii) Zinc carbonate on heating gives zinc oxide and carbon dioxide.
(iii) Hydrogen combines with chlorine to form hydrogen chloride.
(c) In the reaction ZnO + C → Zn + CO, identify the substance that is oxidised and the substance that is reduced.
OR
(a) What is rancidity? State two methods used to prevent it.
(b) What is corrosion? Name the conditions required for the rusting of iron and describe an activity to show that both are needed.
(c) What is the black coating formed on silver articles left in air? Name the substance responsible for it.

Light travels from air into glass of refractive index 1.5. If the speed of light in air is 3 × 10⁸ m/s, its speed in glass is:
The heat produced in a 20 Ω resistor when a current of 2 A flows through it for 5 s is:

Assertion (A): The focal length of a concave lens is taken as positive.
Reason (R): A concave lens spreads out a parallel beam of light passing through it.

Assertion (A): Tungsten is used for making the filaments of electric bulbs.
Reason (R): Tungsten has a very high melting point.

A concave lens of focal length 20 cm forms an image at a distance of 10 cm from the lens on the same side as the object. Find the distance of the object from the lens and the magnification. State the nature of the image.

(a) Define the principal focus of a concave mirror.
(b) An object is placed 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position, nature and magnification of the image.

Two resistors of 4 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in parallel, and this combination is connected in series with a 2 Ω resistor and a 6 V battery. Find (a) the equivalent resistance of the circuit, (b) the current drawn from the battery and (c) the current through the 4 Ω resistor.

In a house, an electric heater of 1000 W is used for 2 hours a day and a 100 W bulb is used for 10 hours a day. Calculate (a) the electrical energy consumed in 30 days in kWh and (b) the cost of this energy at ₹6 per kWh.

(a) What is meant by earthing? Why is it necessary for electrical appliances with metallic bodies?
(b) Distinguish between overloading and short-circuiting in a domestic circuit.
(c) What is the function of an electric fuse?

questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text:
A student cannot see objects clearly when they are more than 2 m away.
(a) Name the defect of vision she is suffering from.
(b) State two possible causes of this defect.
(c) Find the nature and power of the lens she needs to see distant objects clearly.

Rohan's grandmother uses a convex lens of focal length 10 cm as a magnifying glass to read the small print on medicine labels. She holds the lens 6 cm above the label and sees a large, clear image of the letters.
(a) What is the power of the lens?
(b) Find the position of the image formed by the lens and state its nature.
(c) Find the magnification produced.
OR
(c) If she holds the lens 20 cm above the label, where will the image be formed and what will be its size compared with the letters?

(a) Describe an activity to show that a current-carrying straight conductor experiences a force when it is placed in a magnetic field.
(b) State Fleming's left-hand rule.
(c) A proton moving horizontally from west to east enters a magnetic field that is directed vertically downwards. In which direction will the proton be deflected?
OR
(a) Draw the pattern of magnetic field lines due to a current-carrying circular loop.
(b) How does the magnetic field at the centre of the loop change if (i) the current is increased and (ii) the number of turns is increased?
(c) What is an electromagnet? State two ways in which its strength can be increased.
